notes: All metadata from Crossref works API; abstracts and full texts from Europe PMC REST (search resultType=core, fullTextXML), NCBI E-utilities efetch (db=pmc) and the PMC article HTML page; software facts from GitHub REST API and PyPI JSON API. No duplicates in batch. Pathmanathan & Gray Crossref record has no page/article number; volume 4 and page 358 come from Europe PMC pageInfo. Scharm et al.: Crossref issued/published-online 2015-10-21, published-print 2016-02-15 (vol 32 issue 4); year recorded as 2016 (issue year) with online date noted.

rows.citation: Gleeson P, Steuber V, Silver RA (2007). neuroConstruct: A Tool for Modeling Networks of Neurons in 3D Space. Neuron 54(2):219-235.
rows.model_type: conductance-based multicompartment neurons and 3D networks described in NeuroML/ChannelML, code-generated for NEURON and GENESIS
rows.controlled_mutations: partial - one sensitivity reference only: Na+ conductance altered by 1% to judge whether simulator differences matter; no mutant set.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - simulator comparison of the granule cell model uses one depolarizing current step; network runs use synaptic input, not a protocol battery.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - final action-potential timing and RMS voltage-trace difference; ISI histograms for network activity; no standardized feature library.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - stimuli chosen by hand; no selection of informative protocols.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - demonstration on a few published models (granule cell, Mainen neuron, granule cell layer network); no discovery/held-out split.
rows.ai_transformations: no - transformations are automatic NeuroML-to-simulator code generation, not AI-assisted edits.
rows.software: neuroConstruct - https://github.com/NeuralEnsemble/neuroConstruct (GitHub API: GPL-2.0, pushed 2026-09-01); paper cites http://www.neuroConstruct.org
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Checks behaviour preservation of NeuroML translation for one step stimulus with time-step convergence and a 1% conductance yardstick. NeuroSem generalizes this into refinement-calibrated tolerances, many single-fault mutants, a selected multi-protocol battery and held-out tests.
rows.verification_method: Crossref https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1016/j.neuron.2007.03.025; Europe PMC core record PMID 17442244 / PMC1885959 (abstract) and fullTextXML https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC1885959/fullTextXML (Results section on two-simulator comparison); GitHub REST https://api.github.com/repos/NeuralEnsemble/neuroConstruct

rows.citation: Niederer SA, Kerfoot E, Benson AP, et al. (2011). Verification of cardiac tissue electrophysiology simulators using an N-version benchmark. Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A: Mathematical, Physical and Engineering Sciences 369(1954):4331-4351.
rows.model_type: cardiac tissue monodomain PDE with ten Tusscher & Panfilov epicardial ionic cell model on a 3x7x20 mm cuboid
rows.controlled_mutations: no - no seeded faults; discrepancies among 11 independent codes are observed, not injected.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - one benchmark with a single corner stimulus; variation is over 3 spatial x 3 time resolutions.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - single metric: activation time (0 mV crossing) at fixed points and along lines through the tissue.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - one hand-designed benchmark problem; authors note richer benchmarks could reveal more differences.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - all 11 codes compared on the same benchmark to form a consensus solution; no held-out codes or models.
rows.ai_transformations: no - independently developed human-written simulation codes.
rows.software: none (benchmark definition and supplementary activation-time data; codes anonymized A-K in results)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Verifies whole simulators against a refined consensus on one benchmark and one metric. NeuroSem targets edits to individual neuron models, with injected single faults, multiple stimuli, eFEL features, protocol selection and held-out evaluation.
rows.verification_method: Crossref https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1098/rsta.2011.0139; Europe PMC core record PMID 21969679 / PMC3263775 (abstract); PMC article HTML https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3263775/ (methods: geometry, stimulus, resolutions, activation-time metric)

rows.citation: Pathmanathan P, Gray RA (2013). Ensuring reliability of safety-critical clinical applications of computational cardiac models. Frontiers in Physiology 4:358.
rows.model_type: cardiac electrophysiology cell and tissue models (general VVUQ discussion)
rows.controlled_mutations: no - conceptual article; mentions known-solution problems for solver verification but no mutant generation.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - discusses validation and uncertainty conceptually; no feature extraction method.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Frames verification (numerical and programming error), validation and uncertainty quantification for cardiac models. NeuroSem is a concrete empirical regression-testing method for model edits; this is background framing, not an anticipating method.
rows.verification_method: Crossref https://api.crossref.org/works/10.3389/fphys.2013.00358; Europe PMC core record PMID 24376423 / PMC3858646 (abstract, volume/page) and fullTextXML https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC3858646/fullTextXML

rows.citation: Scharm M, Wolkenhauer O, Waltemath D (2016). An algorithm to detect and communicate the differences in computational models describing biological systems. Bioinformatics 32(4):563-570.
rows.model_type: SBML and CellML model versions (XML-encoded systems biology / physiology models); NeuroML named only as possible extension
rows.controlled_mutations: no - diffs real coexisting model versions; no seeded faults.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - purely structural comparison; models are not simulated.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - compares encoding, network structure and mathematical expressions, not simulated behaviour.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - no held-out design; evaluated against standard XML diff approaches.
rows.software: BiVeS - https://github.com/SemsProject/BiVeS (GitHub API: Apache-2.0, last push 2021-05-10); paper cites sems.uni-rostock.de and BudHat web interface
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Reports what changed structurally between versions, ignoring whitespace and attribute order. NeuroSem asks whether behaviour changed, via simulation under several stimuli; structural diffs could complement it but cannot detect silent drift.
rows.verification_method: Crossref https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1093/bioinformatics/btv484; Europe PMC core record PMID 26490504 / PMC4743622 (abstract) and fullTextXML https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC4743622/fullTextXML; GitHub REST https://api.github.com/repos/SemsProject/BiVeS

rows.citation: Tiwari K, Kananathan S, Roberts MG, et al. (2021). Reproducibility in systems biology modelling. Molecular Systems Biology 17(2):MSB20209982.
rows.model_type: published ODE kinetic systems biology models encoded in SBML (BioModels curation)
rows.controlled_mutations: no - errors found in published models were natural reporting errors, some corrected manually; nothing seeded.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - each model checked against the simulation figures in its original paper.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - kinetic model outputs compared with published figures; not electrophysiology.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - retrospective analysis of 455 curation-prioritized models; no split.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Shows about half of 455 published ODE models did not directly reproduce and proposes an 8-point scorecard. Motivates behaviour checks but offers no automated edit-regression method; NeuroSem supplies one for neuron models.
rows.verification_method: Crossref https://api.crossref.org/works/10.15252/msb.20209982; Europe PMC core record PMID 33620773 / PMC7901289 (abstract) and fullTextXML https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC7901289/fullTextXML

rows.citation: Lieven C, Beber ME, Olivier BG, et al. (2020). MEMOTE for standardized genome-scale metabolic model testing. Nature Biotechnology 38(3):272-276.
rows.controlled_mutations: no - no seeded faults; tests flag real defects such as stoichiometric inconsistency or blocked reactions.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - biomass production tested under different conditions; users may add growth and gene-perturbation experiment tests.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - annotation, stoichiometry and biomass/flux tests, not electrophysiology.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - fixed consensus test library; no selection of a compact informative subset.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - no held-out evaluation of detection power.
rows.software: memote - https://github.com/opencobra/memote (GitHub API and PyPI: Apache-2.0; PyPI latest 0.17.0)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: A standardized test suite with version-control history and diff reports tracking each model edit, close to OMV in spirit. It tests quality rather than behaviour preservation, and does no mutation calibration, protocol selection or held-out evaluation, which NeuroSem would add for neuron models.
rows.verification_method: Crossref https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1038/s41587-020-0446-y; Europe PMC core record PMID 32123384 / PMC7082222 (no abstract text returned); NCBI efetch https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/efetch.fcgi?db=pmc&id=7082222 (author-manuscript full text); GitHub REST README https://api.github.com/repos/opencobra/memote/readme; PyPI https://pypi.org/pypi/memote/json
